official.deadline_central_display: Accept the admission offer and pay the tuition fee (or first instalment) within 21 days of the admission results; annual tuition by 31 August in later years
official.deadline_note: There is no separate scholarship deadline. The Early Bird discount depends on accepting the offer and paying within the deadline in the admission letter, usually 21 days after results; from the second year the annual tuition must be paid by 31 August, in one payment or two equal instalments.
official.application_cycle: 2027 intake (page updated 3 August 2026); the annual tuition cycle runs 1 August to 31 July
official.status_note: UEF publishes its tuition waivers for the 2027 intake on this page: a 30% Early Bird discount for the first academic year, a 30% progress-based waiver for subsequent years, and Finnish Proficiency Tuition Waivers, with a separate application period after the first year of studies.
official.tuition_coverage_note: "UEF's tuition waiver programme is designed to provide partial support towards tuition fees. Applicants cannot apply for full (100%) tuition waivers." The exception is students granted temporary protection, who are eligible for a 100% tuition fee waiver.
official.funding_period: one-off on first academic year tuition
benefits: Early Bird discount of 30% of the first academic year's tuition fee (EUR 3,000 on a EUR 10,000 fee, EUR 3,600 on a EUR 12,000 fee)
30% tuition waiver for the second and third year of bachelor's studies and the second year of master's studies, based on at least 55 ECTS in the first year
Finnish Proficiency Tuition Waiver A, value EUR 2,500, on a certificate of Finnish language proficiency
Finnish Proficiency Tuition Waiver B, value EUR 1,500, on studies completed at UEF
100% tuition fee waiver for students admitted to an English-taught programme who have been granted temporary protection by the Finnish Immigration Service
eligibility: Citizen from outside the EU/EEA area or Switzerland, liable to pay tuition fees
Admitted to a UEF international Bachelor's or Master's degree programme for the 2027 intake
Early Bird: accept the offer of admission and pay the tuition fee or first instalment within 21 days of the admission results
Later-year waiver: complete at least 55 ECTS credits during the first academic year (1 August to 31 July) included in the degree and approved as part of the Personal Study Plan
requirements: Pay the application fee required of applicants from outside the EU, EEA or Switzerland; it cannot be waived and does not apply to Erasmus Mundus programmes
Accept the admission offer and pay by the deadline in the admission letter to obtain the Early Bird discount
Apply for the second-year waiver in the separate application period organised after the first year of studies
Apply only once for a Finnish Proficiency Tuition Waiver, in its own separate application period
Have a residence permit valid at the start of the academic year, i.e. 1 August, to keep the fee exemption
documents: Copies of both sides of a valid Finnish residence permit card
A copy of a valid passport or national ID card indicating citizenship
Proof of admission to a UEF international degree programme for the 2027 intake
For the temporary-protection waiver, proof of temporary protection or evidence that the application is pending
selection_criteria: The Early Bird discount is granted on timely payment, not on academic assessment
The 30% waiver for later years is awarded at the same rate to all students who meet the 55 ECTS eligibility criteria
Only studies completed while enrolled as a degree student at UEF are counted, as a general rule
Faculties may additionally award discretionary merit-based scholarships for outstanding academic achievement
coverage: Early Bird discount of 30% of the first-year tuition fee
30% of the annual tuition fee in the second and subsequent study years, based on academic progress
Finnish Proficiency Tuition Waivers of EUR 2,500 and EUR 1,500
No coverage of living expenses; the university states students must have sufficient personal funds
application_method: Apply to the UEF international degree programme and pay the application fee where required
Accept the admission offer and pay the tuition fee or first instalment through Flywire within 21 days of the results to secure the 30% Early Bird discount
Enclose residency documents with the application where an exemption from tuition fees is claimed
After the first academic year, apply for the 30% waiver and, once eligible, for a Finnish Proficiency Tuition Waiver in their own application periods
official.application_route: Apply for admission, then accept and pay within 21 days of the results through Flywire; later-year waivers need their own application after the first year of studies.
official.study_mode: Full-time study in an international Bachelor's or Master's degree programme taught in English
official.citizenship_residency: Fees and waivers apply to citizens outside the EU/EEA area and Switzerland; certain Finnish permit types (P, P-EU, EU Blue Card, Brexit, temporary protection and some A permits) exempt a student from fees entirely.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the scheme exists for non-EU/EEA and non-Swiss students in UEF's international Bachelor's and Master's programmes.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Erasmus Mundus and joint degree programmes have their own tuition fee and scholarship programmes and are outside UEF's waiver system.
official.duration: The Early Bird discount covers the first academic year; the 30% waiver covers the second and subsequent study years for the duration of the study right
official.description: The University of Eastern Finland charges EUR 10,000-12,000 per academic year to students from outside the EU/EEA area and Switzerland in its international Bachelor's and Master's programmes, and offers partial support only: a 30% Early Bird discount for the first academic year, a 30% progress-based waiver for later years and Finnish Proficiency Tuition Waivers. UEF states that applicants cannot apply for full waivers and that it offers no scholarships on humanitarian grounds.
official.program_type: Early Bird tuition discount and academic-progress tuition waiver

verification.notes: Read the University of Eastern Finland tuition fees, waivers and scholarships page in full, including the 2027 intake Early Bird and waiver terms, the Finnish Proficiency waivers, the temporary protection waiver, the exemption criteria and the refund policy. The EUR 3,000/EUR 3,600 Early Bird figures and the EUR 2,500/EUR 1,500 proficiency values are quoted from that page.

applicant_utility.summary: The money here is earned by paying on time and then by studying fast: 30% off the first year if you pay within 21 days of the results, another 30% in later years if you bank at least 55 ECTS in year one, plus EUR 2,500 or EUR 1,500 once for reaching Finnish language proficiency. There is no full waiver for ordinary applicants - UEF says so directly - so plan for EUR 7,000-8,400 of tuition a year plus living costs on top. The one genuine route to 100% is temporary protection granted by Migri, which UEF will even grant provisionally while your application is pending.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Non-EU/EEA applicants to UEF's English-taught programmes who can pay tuition promptly and who are willing to learn Finnish to unlock the proficiency waivers.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your programme is not an Erasmus Mundus or joint programme, which follow their own fee and scholarship rules
Have the full first-year fee ready as a single payment, or plan two equal instalments with the second due by 31 August
Have residence permit card and passport copies ready to enclose if you claim a fee exemption
Plan the first year around 55 ECTS of credits that sit inside your Personal Study Plan, not just any credits
Note the separate application periods for the later-year waiver and the Finnish Proficiency waivers
Budget EUR 900-1,000 a month for living costs, above the EUR 800 Migri minimum
common_rejection_risks: Paying later than 21 days after results, which forfeits the entire first-year discount
Completing fewer than 55 ECTS in the first academic year, which ends eligibility for the 30% later-year waiver
Counting credits that were not included in the degree or approved in the Personal Study Plan
Counting credits earned while not enrolled as a UEF degree student, which as a general rule do not count
Assuming a humanitarian or needs-based waiver exists, which UEF explicitly does not offer
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Living expenses for the whole degree - UEF recommends EUR 900-1,000 a month and warns that part-time work is not a reliable source of funding - plus the 70% of tuition the waivers do not cover, the non-waivable application fee, and any fifth-semester costs if the degree runs long.
document_audit: The Early Bird discount is triggered by the payment record through Flywire, so no separate scholarship form exists
Residency verification requires copies of both sides of the residence permit card plus a passport or national ID
The refund request for the first year's tuition must be made by 31 December of the admission year
An Early Bird price paid and later refunded cannot be transferred or used later, even if you re-enrol
alerts: A second instalment paid in August still requires the first instalment inside the 21-day window to keep the discount
If your residence permit status changes mid-year, the effect starts the following academic term and fees already paid are not refunded
All waivers and scholarships are reported to the Finnish Tax Administration
The Early Bird discount is lost if you pay and then renounce the study place to accept one in another country, with no refund
UEF reviews tuition fees annually, so the EUR 10,000-12,000 range can change
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Admission application with the application fee, then accept and pay within 21 days through Flywire, then a post-first-year application window for the 30% waiver, then a one-off Finnish Proficiency waiver application.
